content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for logging strategy work: a short set of checks to run before calling a logging strategy task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When logging strategy decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. When logging strategy guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Validate logging strategy outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. When multiple logging strategy strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Before starting logging strategy work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to logging strategy (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep logging strategy changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen logging strategy approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Prefer the simplest logging strategy approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. State assumptions about logging strategy explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
11. Document any non-obvious logging strategy decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic logging strategy advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting logging strategy assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of logging strategy correctness.
- Do not silently drop logging strategy edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated logging strategy concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about logging strategy over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
